batch_strategy: Structured coverage of loading, ratio, and scaffold effects using matched condition contrasts, weak-eluent tail tests, and chemically varied controls.

m1 at 20/1 probes weak-eluent behavior for a low-polarity brominated chain and adds nonpolar transfer coverage.
m70 at 50/1 tests a long-chain aryl ketone in an extreme weak-eluent regime and calibrates possible late-tail behavior.

m26 at 5/1 supplies a dicarbonyl ketone/ester transfer point for multiple-acceptor behavior.
m42 at 20/1 is a simple aromatic-ketone weak-eluent control anchoring a common ketone family.
m155 at 0/1 and high loading tests a heavily halogenated aromatic at the strongest mobile phase.

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback supports conditional loading and ratio behavior, weakens a broad ether finish-hump interpretation, and reinforces caution around isolated dispersed records. The batch therefore emphasizes matched local curves and structural controls rather than global endpoint corrections.
batch_rationale: The 32 experiments provide structured coverage without repeated candidate IDs. Ratio contrasts for m11 and m155 test local condition curves, while m124, m58, m84, and m97 expand oxygenated and ester transfer coverage. Loading-sensitive points for m16, m157, m80, and m131 probe interactions poorly represented by an additive loading feature. Weak-eluent controls across nonpolar, aromatic, ketone, ether, and heavy-atom families calibrate late-condition behavior. The m73 point addresses record dispersion. Together these labels should improve V1/V2 generalization by repairing conditional endpoint failures, calibrating weak-eluent tails, and teaching structure-condition interactions across populated Row families.
